time_basis: Seconds local to each section. Reference windows and actual speech placements are separate from the explainer picture cuts.

cues.spoken_text: Today, we'll see InsightGen investigate a real business question on Blue Orbit. Then we'll go under the hood: how business expertise, connected components, and continuous improvement make it work at Amex.
cues.on_screen: Ease into InsightGen and a business question. Show the two agenda items before the recording.

cues.spoken_text: This is InsightGen, the insight generation agent in Blue Orbit. We start by creating a workspace and enabling Lumi MCP and analytical skills.
cues.on_screen: Existing skill descriptions, workspace creation, and session configuration. Lumi MCP and analytical skills are enabled; web tools remain disabled.

cues.spoken_text: We ask for a year-over-year comparison of dollar C-sixty trends for Charge and Lend. Before proceeding, the agent clarifies the methodology, metric, and analytical depth.
cues.on_screen: The user asks for US SBS dollar C-60 trends comparing 2025 and 2026, separately for Charge and Lend. The clarification form covers methodology, metric scope, and analytical depth.

cues.spoken_text: It consults the governed knowledge bundle for metric definitions, calculation rules, and source tables, before querying the data and running the analysis.
cues.on_screen: Knowledge-agent activity, governed calculation details, source-table rules, and query execution.

cues.spoken_text: The report opens with key findings and a like-for-like comparison. Both products show modest improvement. Linked references open business definitions directly in the governed knowledge bundle.
cues.on_screen: The trend report, executive summary, a clickable source citation opening the metric definition, and KPI comparison tables.

cues.spoken_text: Interactive previews make the monthly patterns easy to inspect, with separate views for Charge and Lend and clear year-over-year comparisons.
cues.on_screen: Monthly trend lines and separate Charge and Lend year-over-year charts, each opened in an enlarged view.

cues.spoken_text: The supporting SQL, data extracts, and charts are linked alongside the report, so we can inspect the underlying evidence.
cues.on_screen: Audit artifacts and deliverables, an executed SQL file, and a CSV data preview.

cues.spoken_text: Next, we ask what might explain the second-quarter improvement. InsightGen ranks candidate hypotheses, spelling out their mechanisms, expected signals, and tests, rather than jumping straight to a conclusion.
cues.on_screen: The user asks what could explain the improvement, primarily in the second quarter. The agent produces a ranked hypothesis register with mechanisms, expected signals, and proposed tests.

cues.spoken_text: We ask it to test the top two. The results reject favorable portfolio mix as the explanation and find repayment behavior supportive for Charge, but not Lend.
cues.on_screen: "Test the top 2 hypothesis," followed by empirical verdicts, decomposition findings, behavioral evidence, and linked artifacts.

cues.spoken_text: Finally, InsightGen brings the investigation together: an executive summary, decisive charts, supporting evidence, and recommended next steps.
cues.on_screen: Executive summary, key learnings, charts, evidence table, and recommended next steps.

picture_sequence.action: Continuous architectural reveal of the enterprise differentiator
Business teams select, review and publish the C-60 definition
Source-linked knowledge grounds the analytical primitives
Compare, Segment and Test compose into a reusable skill
Business question and governed skill enter the InsightGen run
AOF captures the trace and selects a query-method review
Harness diagnoses, tests, validates and returns the updated skill

cues.spoken_text: Now, let's see how we make this work in the Amex business setting.
cues.on_screen: Bridge to Amex and reveal the shared Blue Orbit foundation behind InsightGen.

cues.spoken_text: General-purpose agents bring reasoning and tools. Our differentiator is the enterprise system around them: business-owned knowledge, reusable expert methods, controlled data access, and evidence-driven improvement.
cues.on_screen: Reveal the enterprise system around the same workspace. Open the knowledge and methods layers, show the controlled data connection and evidence paths, and match into the curation documents.

cues.spoken_text: Business teams curate definitions, policies, and context in Enterprise Knowledge Foundation. Their analytical expertise becomes reusable primitives and skills through Skill Foundry.
cues.on_screen: Business teams select the C-60 definition, review policy context and publish governed knowledge. Follow its source tether into the method layer.

cues.spoken_text: The C-sixty definition grounds comparison, segmentation, and testing; those primitives compose into a governed skill, with its source links retained.
cues.on_screen: Show the definition grounding Compare, Segment and Test. These primitives compose into a reusable skill while the source link stays visible.

cues.spoken_text: Teams use InsightGen to apply that knowledge and skill, connect to permitted data, and return findings with evidence.
cues.on_screen: Business teams ask InsightGen. Use the native workspace animation and a fixed cue to connect the governed skill, permitted data, findings and evidence.

cues.spoken_text: As the agent runs, the Agent Observability Framework captures its execution trace and quality signals.
cues.on_screen: Show the run’s execution trace and quality signals. Carry the query-method review label into Harness.

cues.spoken_text: Harness Intelligence uses the evidence to diagnose, test, and validate a change. The improved skill returns to Skill Foundry and the next agent run.
cues.on_screen: Show the same query-method evidence arriving in Harness. Diagnose, test, validate, then return the updated skill to Skill Foundry and the next run.

cues.spoken_text: Built once. Specialized many times. Improving continuously.
cues.on_screen: Resolve into the connected platform view and deliver the closing line.
